summary.one_liner: eza is a modern, colourful replacement for the Unix `ls` file-listing command, distributed as a single binary.
summary.what_it_does: eza lists directory contents with colours for file types and metadata, and understands symlinks, extended attributes, and Git status. It offers display modes such as one-per-line, grid, long details, recursive, and tree views. Filtering options include hidden-file display, depth limits, glob-based ignores, .gitignore support, and directories-only or files-only listing. The long view adds options for sizes, timestamps (modified, accessed, created, changed, with several time styles), permissions in octal, inodes, hard links, SELinux context, mount details, and Git status per file or per repo. Appearance can be customized through a theme.yml file for colours and icons, and the README says it also supports hyperlinks and a `--stdin` option for reading file names.
use_cases: replace ls with a more readable file listing
show Git status next to files in a directory
display a directory as a tree
list files sorted by size or modification date
customize ls colours and icons with a theme file
inspect file permissions, inodes, or SELinux context
how_to_run: See INSTALL.md for platform and distribution-specific installation instructions
notable: Successor to exa, with fixes such as 'The Grid Bug' and several security fixes
Git status output for files and directories, including a faster no-status mode
theme.yml configuration for colours and icons, with pre-made themes in a separate eza-themes repository
Mount point details (Linux and macOS) and SELinux context output
caveats: Mount details (-M) are available only on Linux and macOS
README says the feature list is non-exhaustive and does not give full details; users are pointed to the man pages
